title: How the Neuroblast Picks a Side

scenes.visual: Title card: How the Neuroblast Picks a Side.

scenes.tts: The bristle showed what an inherited protein does. But how does a cell put it on one side?
scenes.visual: A neuroblast with a question mark on its cortex. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: The bristle showed what an inherited protein does. But how does a cell put it on one side?

scenes.tts: The fly neuroblast is where that machinery was worked out.
scenes.visual: Map 2 from chapter one: the neuroblast and its small basal daughter. Labels: apical, basal.
scenes.narration: The fly neuroblast is where that machinery was worked out.

scenes.tts: A clue came in nineteen ninety-five. Prospero is a transcription factor, a protein that works in the nucleus.
scenes.caption: A clue came in 1995. Prospero is a transcription factor, a protein that works in the nucleus.
scenes.visual: Date card: 1995. A Prospero icon sits inside a nucleus.
scenes.narration: A clue came in 1995. Prospero is a transcription factor, a protein that works in the nucleus.

scenes.tts: Yet Yurgen Knoblich and the Jans found it at the membrane in dividing cells, in the same crescent as Numb.
scenes.caption: Yet Jürgen Knoblich and the Jans found it at the membrane in dividing cells, in the same crescent as Numb.
scenes.visual: Name card: Knoblich, Jan and Jan, 1995. In a dividing cell, Prospero sits at the membrane beside the gold Numb crescent.
scenes.narration: Yet Jürgen Knoblich and the Jans found it at the membrane in dividing cells, in the same crescent as Numb.

scenes.tts: Its position followed one centrosome, but it did not need microtubules. So it was not carried into place along the spindle.
scenes.visual: The crescent sits near one centrosome. Microtubules fade out, and the crescent stays.
scenes.narration: Its position followed one centrosome, but it did not need microtubules. So it was not carried into place along the spindle.

scenes.tts: That pointed to a separate system in the cortex that marks one side of the cell. It works in four steps.
scenes.visual: A four-step checklist appears at the side: mark the top, aim the spindle, keep the cargo off the top, carry the cargo.
scenes.narration: That pointed to a separate system in the cortex that marks one side of the cell. It works in four steps.

scenes.tts: Step one. Mark the top.
scenes.visual: Checklist step 1 highlights.
scenes.narration: Step one. Mark the top.

scenes.tts: Bazooka, the fly's Par three, gathers at the top cortex.
scenes.caption: Bazooka, the fly's Par3, gathers at the top cortex.
scenes.visual: Bazooka lights up at the apical cortex. Label: Bazooka (Par3).
scenes.narration: Bazooka, the fly's Par3, gathers at the top cortex.

scenes.tts: Par six joins it.
scenes.caption: Par6 joins it.
scenes.visual: Par6 joins the apical patch.
scenes.narration: Par6 joins it.

scenes.tts: So does a kinase called a P K C. Together they define the top side.
scenes.caption: So does a kinase called aPKC. Together they define the top side.
scenes.visual: aPKC joins the apical patch. Label: the apical side is defined.
scenes.narration: So does a kinase called aPKC. Together they define the top side.

scenes.visual: Hold on the reveal.

scenes.tts: Step two. Aim the spindle.
scenes.visual: Checklist step 2 highlights. The spindle sits sideways in the cell.
scenes.narration: Step two. Aim the spindle.

scenes.tts: Inscuteable joins the top complex. Inscuteable recruits a protein called Pins.
scenes.visual: Inscuteable appears at the apical patch, then Pins.
scenes.narration: Inscuteable joins the top complex. Inscuteable recruits a protein called Pins.

scenes.tts: Pins works with a G protein subunit, G alpha i, and a protein called Mud.
scenes.caption: Pins works with a G protein subunit, Gαi, and a protein called Mud.
scenes.visual: Gαi, then Mud, appear beside Pins.
scenes.narration: Pins works with a G protein subunit, Gαi, and a protein called Mud.

scenes.tts: Together they anchor the motor dynein at the top. Dynein pulls on microtubules from one spindle pole.
scenes.visual: Dynein motors anchor at the apical cortex and pull on astral microtubules from the nearer spindle pole.
scenes.narration: Together they anchor the motor dynein at the top. Dynein pulls on microtubules from one spindle pole.

scenes.tts: So the spindle lines up from top to bottom. The furrow will cut between top and bottom.
scenes.visual: The spindle swings to the apical-basal axis.
scenes.narration: So the spindle lines up from top to bottom. The furrow will cut between top and bottom.

scenes.tts: Inscuteable is needed both to aim the spindle and to place Numb and Prospero correctly.
scenes.visual: Inset: without Inscuteable, the spindle is misaimed and the crescents are misplaced.
scenes.narration: Inscuteable is needed both to aim the spindle and to place Numb and Prospero correctly.

scenes.visual: Hold on the reveal.

scenes.tts: Step three. Keep the cargo off the top.
scenes.visual: Checklist step 3 highlights. Numb and Miranda sit all around the cortex; Lgl, a helper, sits there too.
scenes.narration: Step three. Keep the cargo off the top.

scenes.tts: At the top, a P K C phosphorylates L G L, Numb and Miranda.
scenes.caption: At the top, aPKC phosphorylates Lgl, Numb and Miranda.
scenes.visual: aPKC adds phosphate tags to Lgl, Numb and Miranda on the apical side.
scenes.narration: At the top, aPKC phosphorylates Lgl, Numb and Miranda.

scenes.tts: Phosphorylated proteins let go of the cortex. And a P K C works only at the top.
scenes.visual: At the apical side only, tagged proteins detach from the cortex into the cytoplasm. No arrows point downward.
scenes.narration: Phosphorylated proteins let go of the cortex. And a P K C works only at the top.

scenes.tts: So Numb and Miranda stay bound only at the bottom cortex. L G L is a helper here, not cargo.
scenes.visual: Separately, Numb and Miranda are shown enriched on the basal cortex, where they can stay bound. Lgl is labelled helper, not cargo.
scenes.narration: So Numb and Miranda stay bound only at the bottom cortex. L G L is a helper here, not cargo.

scenes.tts: Step four. Carry the cargo.
scenes.visual: Checklist step 4 highlights.
scenes.narration: Step four. Carry the cargo.

scenes.tts: The adaptor Miranda carries Prospero, and the translational repressor Brat.
scenes.visual: Miranda at the basal cortex holds Prospero and Brat.
scenes.narration: The adaptor Miranda carries Prospero, and the translational repressor Brat.

scenes.tts: Numb uses its own adaptor, Partner of Numb.
scenes.visual: Numb at the basal cortex with its adaptor, labelled Partner of Numb (Pon).
scenes.narration: Numb uses its own adaptor, Partner of Numb.

scenes.tts: The cell divides. The small daughter, the ganglion mother cell, inherits the cargo.
scenes.visual: The cell divides. The small basal daughter, labelled GMC, takes Numb, Miranda, Prospero and Brat.
scenes.narration: The cell divides. The small daughter, the ganglion mother cell, inherits the cargo.

scenes.tts: Prospero enters its nucleus and shuts down genes for self-renewal and division.
scenes.visual: Close-up of the GMC: Prospero enters the nucleus; genes labelled self-renewal and division switch off.
scenes.narration: Prospero enters its nucleus and shuts down genes for self-renewal and division.

scenes.tts: Now remove Miranda. Where do Prospero and Brat go? What happens over many divisions?
scenes.visual: Prompt card: Lose Miranda. The neuroblast with Prospero and Brat drawn loose in the cytoplasm.
scenes.narration: Now remove Miranda. Where do Prospero and Brat go? What happens over many divisions?

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: They lose their crescent at the bottom cortex. Where they end up depends on the stage and the lineage.
scenes.visual: Reveal: Prospero and Brat are no longer in a basal crescent. Label: their localization then depends on stage and lineage.
scenes.narration: They lose their crescent at the bottom cortex. Where they end up depends on the stage and the lineage.

scenes.tts: Larval miranda mutant tissue overgrows when transplanted. Faulty sorting can let small daughters keep dividing like neuroblasts.
scenes.visual: Labelled context: larval miranda mutant brain tissue, transplanted. Over several divisions, some small daughters divide like neuroblasts. A counter of dividing cells climbs.
scenes.narration: Larval miranda mutant tissue overgrows when transplanted. Faulty sorting can let small daughters keep dividing like neuroblasts.

scenes.visual: Hold on the reveal.

scenes.tts: The sensory organ precursor divides within its epithelium. The neuroblast divides across it.
scenes.visual: Split screen: the SOP dividing in the plane of the epithelium; the neuroblast dividing at right angles to it.
scenes.narration: The sensory organ precursor divides within its epithelium. The neuroblast divides across it.

scenes.tts: But both mark one side and aim the spindle at it.
scenes.visual: Both cells show a gold crescent with the spindle pointing at it.
scenes.narration: But both mark one side and aim the spindle at it.

scenes.tts: Mark the top, aim the spindle, keep the cargo off the top, and load the small daughter.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the four steps, with the small daughter loaded.
scenes.narration: Mark the top, aim the spindle, keep the cargo off the top, and load the small daughter.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
